recommended_approach: Pre-fractured glass shard objects + Rigid Body World: create the window as many irregular shard meshes, assign the shards as Active rigid bodies, keep the steel frame/wall as Passive rigid bodies, and use higher world accuracy settings so the fast brick impact produces a violent outward burst and secondary collapse.

key_parameters.Substeps Per Frame: Higher than default for accuracy on the fast brick impact and many small shard collisions.
key_parameters.Solver Iterations: Higher than default for more stable shard-to-shard and shard-to-frame contacts.
key_parameters.shape: Use a rigid body collision shape appropriate for shards; docs surface Mesh and Convex Hull as the relevant options.
key_parameters.Translation: Keep damping low so shards preserve outward velocity after impact.
key_parameters.Rotation: Keep damping low so shards continue visible tumbling/spin.
key_parameters.Animated: Enable when a rigid body is driven by keyframes; docs warn that a keyframed Passive object without Animated is treated as static by the solver.
key_parameters.Deactivation: Use for the settling phase; docs expose a dedicated Deactivation section for rigid body dynamics.
key_parameters.size: Enable when using a particle-instanced secondary splinter pass so instances scale by particle size.
key_parameters.show_unborn: Only enable for particle-instanced debris if pre-birth visibility is needed.

warnings: Rigid Body is the correct primary physics system for this effect; the retrieved non-rigid-body results were mostly irrelevant for the core break.
The docs explicitly warn that if a Passive rigid body is keyframed without Animated enabled, it may move visually while the physics solver still treats it as static at its original pose.
Higher Substeps Per Frame and Solver Iterations improve accuracy/stability but increase simulation cost.
Retrieved documentation did not surface a strong dedicated Cell Fracture page, so fracture preprocessing may need to be done manually or via add-on workflow outside the retrieved rigid body docs.
Pattern search returned no direct glass-shatter or rigid-body destruction fix pattern, so there is no proven library snippet to reuse here.
The particle-based alternative returned weak API grounding/no valid API doc refs, so it is best treated as a secondary embellishment layer rather than the core break simulation.
alternative_approaches: Hybrid approach: keep hero shards as rigid bodies, then add a Particle Instance Modifier pass for tiny secondary splinters/dust that would be too expensive to simulate as full rigid bodies.
Manual pre-cut shard layout instead of automated fracture preprocessing: model irregular shard pieces ahead of time, then assign rigid bodies and tune world/collision settings for the impact.
Constraint-assisted variation: use rigid body constraints/common-options workflow to keep some remaining pane pieces attached briefly, then release them for the delayed collapse.
